note: Paris SS27 womenswear begins this date. Houses that have not shown are recorded at their latest completed collection.

collections.theme: The desire to belong to a more glamorous world, and the audacity to remake that world in one's own image
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Gucci read as a house that began in respectability and moved toward eccentricity, danger, and sex appeal.
- Late-1980s and early-1990s Gucci man: inherited privilege worn as nonchalance.
- Tom Ford-era body-conscious jersey as the evening memory.

Show / location context:
- Spring/Summer 2027, Milan. Demna's first show presented as his complete personal vision after one year at the house.
- Staged inside The Store, a built replica of a Gucci boutique. Shopping is the spectacle.

Creative director intent:
- Gucci stands for the desire to belong to a more glamorous world, and the audacity to remake that world in one's own image.
- The collection is a cast, not one muse: horse-riding princess, Milanese sciura, prep-school brat, nightclub siren, old-money gentleman, socialite.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Men's opening: slick slim suits, cropped trousers, bare ankles, 1970s open shirting, then prep peacoat and trench, then extra-large suiting and enlarged shoulders.
- Trench with miniature horseshoes on the collar ends. Extra-oversize black overcoat.
- Evening: slinky jersey dresses, sharply cut black dresses, champagne draping, a one-shoulder gown held by a teardrop metal weight, a thigh-high slit, a side cutout from breast to hip.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Tailoring cloth beside fluid jersey. Metal used as a working weight, not as a logo plaque. Glamour should look slightly precarious.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Black, champagne, baby-blue enlarged shirting. Color serves the character. It is not the identity by itself.

Accessories & finishing:
- Handbags are part of the character, carried as if just chosen in the boutique. Loafers with cropped trousers. Horseshoe charms limited to the trench collar.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- Belonging is something you put on. Bourgeois ease and overt seduction share one house. The wearer remakes the glamorous world rather than visiting it.

collections.theme: The Skirt: one familiar garment held as a frame, then contradicted
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Miuccia Prada has long treated the skirt as her equivalent of the T-shirt: simple, primary, able to carry many ideas.
- She calls it a rectangle, a frame, a painting, and a contradiction.
- Crystal skirts recall the house's jeweled skirts of 2008 and 2010.

Show / location context:
- Spring/Summer 2027 womenswear, 22 September 2026, Fondazione Prada. The set reuses the men's lightbox floor.
- Every look includes a skirt. The lineup is a study of about sixty variations on one garment. The house title is The Skirt.

Creative director intent:
- Use the skirt as a raw material and a framework, not as a trend item.
- Narrow the parameter so material, function, embellishment, distance from the body, and the piece worn above it become visible.
- Raf Simons: the same skirt can be sexy, luxurious, for work, or at ease. The combinations are illogical on purpose.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- One graphic, linear skirt silhouette, from mini to midi, pencil to pleat. Some skirts are large enough to be held in the hand like a ballgown. One floral skirt is slit to the hip.
- Above the skirt: a corporate shirt, a satin bra top, a sweater, a nylon raincoat.
- Visible crinoline can cage a pleated skirt or sit outside it. Overlapping pleats can expose enlarged snaps.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Contrasting Velcro is both fastening and a ground for crystal embroidery, and it can be opened to change the shape.
- Enlarged metal snaps become jeweled.
- Crinoline leaves the inside and becomes a shell.
- Re-Nylon and ciré are pleated. Treated cotton resembles leather or suede. Crystal rebuilds lace. One skirt can be almost pure chandelier crystal. Drab menswear wool and pale peach crepe de chine with a scalloped hem both appear.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Neon fastening panels, vivid floral prints, Sixties "stupid little flowers," and drab wool. Color is one of the contradictions, not a separate story.

Accessories & finishing:
- The jewels are the snaps and the crystal on the closure. Do not add a separate jewelry story that leaves the skirt.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- Freedom is being able to wear one known garment in incompatible ways. The wearer questions whether newness requires a shape nobody has seen.

collections.theme: Craft kept as the logo, lightened into a wearable in-between
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Intrecciato is the house mark, as distinctive as a monogram. Louise Trotter calls Bottega a house of craft, and says craft is the logo.
- This is her third collection, and the first in which her own handwriting is fully visible.

Show / location context:
- Spring/Summer 2027, Milan. The season is treated as a passage: spring opening into summer, layers beginning to fall away.

Creative director intent:
- Find techniques that keep extraordinary handwork while adding lightness and wearability.
- Name the condition in-betweenness: suspended between one state and another, between seasons and between identities.
- A language of polished things beside a language of more organic things. Leave evidence of the hand.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Clothes flutter and barely touch the body while still drawing its contour. Tailoring loosens.
- A longline coat knotted at one side over a light cotton dress. A fringed scarf-belt on a relaxed suit. A basket-weave T-shirt. A scoop-neck leather midi. A macramé tank with a gauzy, lightly pleated maxi skirt.
- Fringe bubble skirts whose hems lift into ellipses while walking. A dress on which fringe draws a trompe-l'oeil floral.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Lighter, crisper cloth; airy lace and crochet from Venetian knitting and stitching; straw, ribbon, leather that has become featherlight.
- An enlarged intrecciato tote that reads as raffia. Crochet overshirts. Fringe on a straw bag long enough to near the floor.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Mostly neutral, with butter yellow, lilac, tangerine, a lavender fringe skirt, and one earthy mixed fringe skirt. Color is a choice inside the craft, not a print story.

Accessories & finishing:
- The hip scarf, the floor-reaching straw fringe, and the raffia-like tote are part of the garment's movement. They are not add-on charms.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- Lightness without relying only on sheer fabric. Imperfection is the proof of making. The clothes are for a life past the show, still poetic.

collections.theme: A second skin, with visibility decided by the wearer
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Maria Grazia Chiuri's second ready-to-wear show for Fendi.
- The line she has been using at the house: Less I. More Us.
- Clothing described by the house as a second skin, porous to emotion.

Show / location context:
- Spring/Summer 2027, Milan, in a hall of mirrors. The audience is separated from the runway and still watching.
- Invitations carry an e. e. cummings line: when I like my body, it is with your body.
- Soundtrack spirit from Raffaella Carrà, with Rumore and Adriano Celentano. Italian sensuality that is theatrical and knowingly camp.

Creative director intent:
- Start one layer closer to the skin. Bras, slips, lace rompers, and bloomers are the architecture worn before an outfit decides what it is.
- Sensuality does not have to mean exposure. The wearer sets the terms.
- A body can be strong and fragile, masculine and feminine, sometimes at once.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Plunge-front sheer midi. A going-out dress whose straps come undone. Salmon-pink lace-trimmed bloomers with a matching bralette. Black polished suiting.
- A slender Napoleonic cape coat over slouchy distressed denim. Plush opera coats.
- Headscarves. Layers stay light on the foot.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Lace, sheer silk, bead, sequin, fringe. The Baguette appears covered in sequins, fringe, and pattern.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Salmon pink against black suiting. Embellishment glints. It should not become a nightclub costume.

Accessories & finishing:
- The Baguette carries the theater. Headscarves frame the face. Straps that can be loosened are part of the garment's control, not damage.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- Getting dressed begins with the body, and the body has the final say. Glamour never costs ease. The shared wardrobe is intimate rather than a slogan.

collections.theme: Entre chien et loup: twilight, where romance and utility share one garment
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Nadège Vanhée has led Hermès womenswear since 2014. Leather and equestrian codes are the house language.
- The collection title is Entre chien et loup, the French name for dusk, when a dog cannot be told from a wolf.
- Show notes invoke Hecate. The clothes stay muscular rather than mythological.

Show / location context:
- Fall/Winter 2026, Paris, built as twilight. Guests met the set by scent before they saw the clothes.
- A later Los Angeles chapter of the same season shifts from outdoor and equestrian exploration toward dance: a dancer leaving rehearsal.

Creative director intent:
- Twilight is a state of mind, not a black palette. Romance and utility are not opposites.
- Zippers and openings let the wearer reconfigure a garment through the day.
- In Los Angeles, the Carré becomes a dress: draped, then constructed. Ballet is grace of gesture and skill, crossed with the craftsman's skill.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Narrow, aerodynamic lines. Fluid overcoats with enormous Tuscan sheepskin collars. Zip-front mini dresses in inky blue that open onto a contrasting shirt. An orange ostrich-leather jumpsuit, belted.
- Jodhpurs, flat-heeled riding boots, glossy lambskin cycling shorts with aviator jackets, long riding coats, leather trenches, double-breasted blazers, cigarette trousers.
- Quilted silk printed with a cloud-strewn sky.
- Los Angeles: Carré dresses, wrap dresses, bustiers drawn from ballet slippers, leather parkas thrown over a performance body, a leather look touched by the American West.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Leather as muscle: ostrich engineered into second-skin jumpsuits and long dresses. Sheepskin collars. Quilted silk as the soft exception. Zips run diagonally or the full length of a dress.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Not simply black. Sulfur yellow, oxblood, forest green, iridescent burgundy, deep blue, moss, charcoal. Surfaces change in the light. A cloud-and-tower print from an Art Deco perspective study.

Accessories & finishing:
- The zip is the finishing. Pockets and openings are functional and visible. Do not add a charm story that leaves the leather.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- Agency: the same coat can open into another hour. Elegance is calibration. The Los Angeles fantasy is a dancer who has just put a jacket on and left the studio.

collections.theme: Super Nature: nature as the first designer, clothing as anthropology
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Nicolas Ghesquière at Louis Vuitton. The house's subject is travel, the monogram, and the trunk.
- He calls nature the greatest designer, and folklore an attempt to explain the forces of nature.

Show / location context:
- Fall/Winter 2026, titled Super Nature. The Cour Carrée of the Louvre was turned into an abstract mountain landscape by Jeremy Hindle, production designer of Severance: verdant prisms and pyramidal peaks, a pastoral scene inside a science-fiction dish.

Creative director intent:
- An anthropology of fashion: what mountain people from the Alps, Central Asia, and the Andes share. Endurance, protection, freedom of movement.
- Architectural clothing that can express different cultures and still bring them together.
- Show a known landscape as if it had never been seen. Wearable pieces stay inside the big scheme.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Shaggy capes, exaggerated and monumental shoulders, fur epaulettes that swallow the arm, cone-shaped hats, shearling caps, walking sticks draped with handbags.
- Cropped leather bombers, rounded cocoon coats, and smaller rounded coats that can actually be worn. Headgear reaches upward.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Fuzzy capes, cowbells, muddy-looking felt, shearling.
- Buttons like minerals. Heels like antlers. Vegetal furs. Leather grained and grooved to mirror wood. Invented leather flowers that decorate and protect.
- Animalier woven into canvas and denim. Craft melded with technology.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Moss, earth, and the green of the set. Pattern is animal and mineral, not a resort stripe. Flora and fauna leave an imprint rather than a cute print.

Accessories & finishing:
- Cowbells, walking sticks, shearling caps.
- Jewels reinterpret Man Ray. Parures studded with the nail-heads of a Louis Vuitton trunk.
- The Noé and other bags shift through time and invite a crossing.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- The wearer is equipped for weather and for moving on. Protection becomes fantastic without ceasing to be clothing. Nomadism is the house, not a backdrop.

collections.theme: A walk in the Tuileries becomes a performance of Dior's archive
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Jonathan Anderson at Christian Dior. He treats the giant past as the necessary start.
- Codes in play: the Bar jacket, the New Look waist and hip, Monsieur Dior's gray, Marc Bohan's monogram, Maria Grazia Chiuri's Book Tote, the framed Dior logo returned toward its original form.

Show / location context:
- Fall/Winter 2026 in the Jardin des Tuileries, spectators behind greenhouse glass. A walk in the park becomes a performance.
- Florals are asked to melt the set and the cloth together, as if water were reflecting off a printed silk.

Creative director intent:
- Redefine Dior's visual language with his own signatures while preserving the codes.
- Hold the real and the unreal in the same hand: garden tactility, then a Paris night and an office blazer.
- Levity matters. The heritage should not become solemn.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Opening: layered tutu skirts with frilled trains, under a textured gray peplum jacket, an ecru organza jacket with floral appliqué and tiny buttons, and a silk feather-printed brocade jacket with a mandarin collar.
- Bar jacket recut with a mandarin collar and rows of miniature buttons, or cropped and double-breasted over masses of hem ruffles.
- Cinched waists. Hips exaggerated with bolts of lace or loose pleats of wool and silk.
- Belle Époque ruffles turned into mini dresses with bouncing trains. Bourgeois tweed, gold-button blazers, shearling with a wave-like hem.
- Heavy evening coats worn slouchy. A blazer with a worn-in jean. Lace panels in eveningwear.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Organza, feather-printed brocade, lace, wool, silk, tweed, shearling, crystallized denim. Printed silk that looks wet.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Emblematic gray. Forest green on a scaled Book Tote. Polka dots. Water-lily and garden florals. Ecru.

Accessories & finishing:
- Water-lily shoes and jewelry. Lily-pad footwear. A green suede turtle bag with button eyes. Marc Bohan monogram as a simple crossbody. Book Tote scaled down and reprinted with the framed logo.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- A Parisian woman who can be in the garden, then at night, without dropping the house line. Play sits on a correct Dior shoulder.

collections.theme: Le Smoking repeated until the shrug becomes the collection
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Yves Saint Laurent's Le Smoking, remembered through Helmut Newton's 1975 Paris Vogue photograph on Rue Aubriot.
- Anthony Vaccarello treats repetition of the house signatures as the definition.

Show / location context:
- Fall/Winter 2026, Paris, at night, inside a simulacrum of a sleek modernist home.
- At the center, an enlarged bust that lived in Yves Saint Laurent's own apartment.
- The woman has a heavy smoked eye and slick, side-parted hair.

Creative director intent:
- Open with eight black trouser suits and close on another. The power suit is an insouciant shrug, not a swagger.
- The protagonist is Romy Schneider in Max et les Ferrailleurs, with the troubled heroines of Gore Vidal and Tennessee Williams beside her.
- Elegance tinged with ennui. The beauty of intimacy and vulnerability.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Black trouser suits with a sloped shoulder, a waist that narrows without constriction, and a plunging neckline.
- Vaccarello's own riff on the tuxedo.
- Sheer lace slips and dresses. Enormous fur coats as the louder counterweight.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Lace coated in silicone, so the slip gains solidity and a curious sheen. It is still transparent and no longer fragile nightwear.
- Fur for volume and confidence against the strict suit.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Black is the code. The silicone adds sheen rather than a second color story. Do not rescue the collection with a bright palette.

Accessories & finishing:
- The bust and the apartment are the scene, not garments to copy onto the body.
- Hair and the smoked eye are the styling that locks the Newton memory. Keep jewelry quieter than the suit and the coated lace.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- A woman who is looked at and slightly tired of it. Glamour includes vulnerability. The suit is both armor and a shrug.

collections.theme: Sous le Salon la Plage: the salon released toward the Biarritz shore
collections.description:
Heritage & provenance:
- Gabrielle Chanel opened her first couture house at Villa Larralde in Biarritz in 1915. The city is where a new female independence, seaside leisure, and social mobility entered the house.
- The meeting with Ernest Beaux and the N°5 lineage. The 1926 black dress as a radical modern classic, here reconsidered through a bow.
- Working-woman dress turned into luxury: marinière stripes, bleu de travail, washed canvas.

Show / location context:
- Cruise 2027, Matthieu Blazy's first Cruise show for Chanel, at Le Casino Municipal in Biarritz. The runway returns to the coastal city rather than treating it as a backdrop.

Creative director intent:
- Liberation as movement between couture and workwear, black dress and swim, structure and ease.
- Heritage is a living laboratory. Classics were once disruptive, then polished until the rebellion looked inevitable.
- The Atlantic is a design source: rhythm, repetition, and touch, not a holiday postcard.

Silhouette & garment vocabulary:
- Structured jackets and black dresses that can leave a salon. Swim and elevated workwear in the same passage.
- Striped seaside graphics, worker-jacket cuts, and architectural detail. A garment should be credible indoors, on a casino terrace, and nearer the water without a costume change.

Materials, craft & surface:
- Tweed, raffia, silk, beaded knit, sequin, canvas. Softness beside precision. Marine shimmer. The Double C reworked as a structural element, not only a plaque.

Color, stripe & graphic codes:
- Black, Basque stripes, marine and shell tones. Stripes operate as architecture and rhythm.

Accessories & finishing:
- Tools for crossing settings: a striped beach panier, bags with waterproof flaps, Art Deco heels, barefoot heel plates, shell earrings, pearls.
- The accessory should make the change of place look elegant.

Mood, liberation & wearer fantasy:
- A woman who owns her pace and does not change costume when the room opens onto the sea. Freedom is wearable. Rebellion has been refined into a classic and should still feel slightly improper.
